column1: # Where each Portuguese noun's gender in lex-pt.tsv was read.
# The tooltip prints a noun's gender beside it, under both forms a row
# weaves. On 2026-10-08 every Portuguese noun was read against English
# Wiktionary's Portuguese entry, fetched raw, and none was wrong: 171 of the
# 178 rows carry the gender of their page's one Portuguese noun, and the 7
# others were read by sense. The same day "evening" became serão, "serão m
# (plural serões or (dated) serãos)", where it had been tarde, f, whose
# A Wiktionary page holds every word of one spelling, so a line citing it
# means the gender of this word's own noun there. Five pages hold more than
# one: coração, heart, is masculine where coração, blushing, is feminine;
# cabeça, head, cobra, snake, and cabra, goat, are feminine beside a
# colloquial noun for a person; and irmã, sister, is feminine beside
# Where Wiktionary gives one word two genders, the seed's is one of them, as
# the Old English and French ledgers have it: bebé, baby, and soldado,
# soldier, are masculine or feminine by the person meant. The seed prints
# tests/tools/genders.test.ts requires every noun in lex-pt.tsv to have a
# line here giving the gender the seed gives, citing the noun's own entry,
# and fails on a line outliving its noun.
